findings.span: If you have acne-prone skin, it can do wonders!
findings.why: In context this implies the cleanser clears or fights acne, an acne-result claim with no substantiation. It also addresses the viewer's skin condition directly, which can draw Meta restrictions (CLM-14).
findings.fix: It's formulated for oily, acne-prone skin.

findings.why: There is a disclosure, but '#Ad' sits only in the last line of a long caption, likely below the 'see more' cut. Disclosure on paid creator content has to be upfront and clearly visible.
findings.fix: Move '#Ad' (or the Paid partnership label) to the first line of the caption.

tone_read: This is a creator ad in the creator's own voice, so brand tone rules don't apply; it is casual, relatable and free of fear hooks. The only policy-relevant line is the acne promise near the end.
language_read: The product is named (Salicylic Acid Cleanser) but without its concentration, which is acceptable in a creator voice. 'Can do wonders' for acne-prone skin is unhedged and implies an acne result, and '#Ad' is placed at the end rather than upfront.
